decisions.reason: As a core hardware launch with high development and commercialization sunk costs and strong public visibility on the home page, it is the kind of product management is likely to continue backing.

This looks like a narrower software add-on with lower sunk costs and weaker public commitment than the hardware and traceability products, making it the easiest offering for management to discontinue if uptake disappointed.

It extends the firm’s established coding business to another important substrate type, so management can readily justify persistence on the basis of fit with the installed base and prior technical investment.

Although it supports digitalization, a mobile decoding app is more peripheral to the firm’s machinery-centered offer and likely carries lower exit costs, so it is comparatively vulnerable to being cut.

Inline code verification is highly consistent with the firm’s stated move toward serialization and end-to-end traceability, which strengthens escalation through strategic commitment as well as product fit.

Because layout software reinforces common operation across systems and was prominently shown on the home page, management is likely to keep supporting it as part of a broader integrated solution strategy.
